body:
> Note that escaping SQL is not always sufficient; table and column names, ORDER BY and so on, cannot be escaped. The inclusion of escaped user-supplied data in these fields results in failed queries or SQL injection.

As this comes just after 5.3.5, it sounds as if it's a warning about the limitations of escaping only, but the same issue applies to parameterized queries. Suggested edit:

> Note that using parameterized queries or escaping SQL is not always sufficient on its own; table and column names, ORDER BY and so on, cannot be parameterized/escaped. The inclusion of escaped user-supplied data in these fields results in failed queries or SQL injection. In these situations, strict input validation (exact-match whitelist) needs to be used too.
title: V5.3 - last sentence applies to parameterized queries too
